stem: A car loan of Rs 3,00,000 is to be repaid in 36 equal monthly instalments under a reducing-balance scheme at 9% per annum compounded monthly. The reducing-balance EMI is: EMI = P x i x (1+i)^n / ((1+i)^n - 1). Given that (1.0075)^36 = 1.3090, what is the monthly EMI?

per_option_rationale.rationale: Uses i = 9%/4 = 2.25% (quarterly rate) instead of monthly 0.75%, inflating EMI to approximately Rs 10,278.
Divides principal by total number of months (300000/36 = 8333) ignoring interest component entirely.
Uses n = 12 (one year) instead of n = 36 (three years) in the formula, giving a higher instalment of approximately Rs 9,167 because the loan term is underestimated.

explanation: Monthly rate i = 9%/12 = 0.0075. With (1.0075)^36 = 1.3090: numerator = 300000 x 0.0075 x 1.3090 = 2945.25; denominator = 0.3090; EMI = 9531 (approximately Rs 9,540).

explanation_sections.punchline: Annual rate must be divided by 12 to get the monthly rate before applying the reducing-balance formula.
explanation_sections.lesson: When the loan tenure is given in months and the rate is annual, always convert: monthly rate = annual rate / 12.
explanation_sections.timing: 75 seconds. Trap: using quarterly rate (9%/4) or ignoring compounding. Ballpark check: Rs 9,540 x 36 = Rs 3,43,440 > Rs 3,00,000, consistent with interest accruing.
